text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cyprus President Glafcos Clerides meets Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash on Monday to discuss humanitarian issues, but with an open agenda.
- The chairman of Cyprus Airways stewards union dismisses suggestions by the company that around 500 members of staff are surplus.
- Shoot-out in Limassol. A policeman was hurt by gunfire in a move against suspected arms dealers.
- The central bank dismisses newspaper reports that the Cyprus pound is ripe for devaluation.
- Communist Akel party will consider a suggestion by Socialist Edek to forge an alliance for the presidential elections now without the centre-left United Democrats.

- Four days after the declaration on the partial integration of the occupied areas with Turkey, Ankara is sending a multi-member delegation to the north today to go over the details of economic integration.
- Three men were arrested after a shootout with police in Limassol during a sting operation to catch illegal arms dealers.

- Socialist Edek wants lawyer Marios Eliades to be the opposition's candidate in the presidential elections. Akel has indicated it is willing to talk about backing former Foreign Minister George Iakovou.
